summary.headline: Camlin Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to about 2.5% as liquidity strain hit margins; board approved a ~INR250 crore rights issue.
summary.overview: Management said the quarter was weak because liquidity constraints forced reliance on channel financing and stretched payables, which raised costs and cut gross margin from INR2,142 million to INR1,958 million. Aroma revenue fell from INR774 million to INR472 million after the switch from methyl vanillin to ethyl vanillin, and the diphenol plant has been closed since May 2026. The board approved a rights issue of about INR250 crore, backed by promoters, to fund working capital, with money expected by end-calendar 2026 or early 2027. Management guided Q3 only marginally better than Q2 and Q4 to over INR600 crore turnover and EBITDA of INR60 crore-plus.

segments.name: Blends (specialty ingredients)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,970 million vs INR3,086 million prior quarter; EBITDA margin about 11-12%, with Europe subsidiaries Vitafor and Vinpai cited as growth levers. Gross margin range 35-40%.

segments.name: Straights (specialty ingredients)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR1,109 million from INR927 million as volumes recovered despite local price competition; average EBITDA margin about 8%.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell to INR472 million from INR774 million after the methyl-to-ethyl vanillin changeover; management cited realisation near $12/kg and an EBITDA of about zero at current selling prices.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (diphenol/hydroquinone)
segments.commentary: Diphenol plant (18,000 MT) closed since May 2026; maintenance cash burn fell to INR5 crore in the quarter from INR8-9 crore, targeted at INR25 million per quarter by end-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27: margin expected to be a tad better than Q2, not a major improvement.
Q4 FY27: turnover above INR6,000 million (INR600 crore) and EBITDA around 10%, or INR60 crore-plus, assuming current raw material prices.
Rights issue of about INR250 crore: pricing, cut-off and issue size to be decided after SEBI/exchange approval of the draft letter of offer; funds expected by end-calendar 2026 or early 2027.
Management says the rights issue could add about INR500 million of blends revenue in Q4 at about 35% gross margin, and about 1,000 MT per quarter of vanillin at about $12/kg.
Management estimated that the rights issue funding could release about INR180-190 crore of interest-related cost (about 3-4% of cost) by unwinding channel financing and overdue payables.
FY27 target of about INR2,000 crore turnover at 10% EBITDA (about INR200 crore) was acknowledged as unlikely by management, confirmed in response to an analyst question.
capex_capacity: Diphenol plant (18,000 MT capacity) closed since May 2026 due to phenol price doubling; no visibility on restart given Chinese capacity pricing well below cost.
Vanillin utilisation: about $10/kg cost at 70% utilisation; management has visibility to run at 70%.
Fixed costs about INR20 crore per quarter, which must be absorbed by volumes.
Vanillin visibility: about 2,500-2,700 MT from the US and 1,300-1,500 MT from Europe for next calendar year; target about 1,000 MT per quarter by Q4 FY27/Q1 next calendar year.
Rights issue proceeds to be used for working capital (about INR130 crore of existing credit), with the rest for growth next calendar year; no further borrowing expected per management.
demand_pricing: Vanillin net realisation about $12-12.5/kg after tariffs and distribution costs; blended ethyl and methyl about $13.7/kg; management says realisation is muted by Chinese material rerouted via Thailand and Malaysia.
Vanillin EBITDA per kg about $2 at 70% utilisation before fixed costs; essentially zero at current volumes.
Raw materials (phenol-linked) have roughly doubled since February; TBHQ and BHA input costs up 15-20%, not passed through due to local competition.
Freight costs almost doubled in the quarter, attributed to the war situation.
Natural blends pricing largely stable; petrochemical-linked blends pass-through lagging. Blends gross margin stays at 35-40%.
Large US distributors reportedly exiting Chinese-origin material due to legal risk; supply starting, expected to grow from Q1 of next calendar year.

qa_highlights.question: What would have been the incremental revenue and gross margin had the rights issue been done a quarter earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales would have been about INR100 crore higher and EBITDA margin about INR60 crore better.

qa_highlights.question: Are promoters participating in the rights issue, and what dilution is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters will subscribe to their share (cited as 48%); pricing not yet decided, so total dilution depends on final pricing expected in the next few weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Why return to B2B distributor channel given credit cycles, and why is vanillin realisation only about $12-12.5?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distributors pay in about 30 days versus 90-120 days for large direct customers, saving working capital; muted realisation reflects rerouted Chinese supply and should improve over three to four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 reach the INR200 crore EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, that is correct, given the H1 run-rate; Q4 is the first quarter with liquidity, with turnaround expected.

qa_highlights.question: How do Aroma EBITDA margin of -23% and $2/kg EBITDA reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $2/kg is at 70% utilisation before about INR20 crore of quarterly fixed costs; at current selling prices and Q2 volumes EBITDA per ton was zero, and the Aroma loss was about INR11 crore on 300 MT after fixed overheads.

qa_highlights.question: How much further capital is needed after the INR250 crore issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the issue should stabilise working capital and fund growth, and no additional borrowings are expected if plans proceed on schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Are there excess inventories in the US vanillin market due to Thailand rerouting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory is being cleared, with destocking expected by year-end.

risks_watch: Liquidity: reliance on channel financing and long-overdue payables (above 90 days carry about 3-4% extra cost); INR250 crore rights issue pricing, timing and final dilution still undetermined.
Q3 guidance is only marginally better than Q2; Q4 turnaround to INR600 crore turnover and 10% EBITDA depends on the rights issue closing on time and raw material prices holding.
Input cost volatility: phenol-linked inputs doubled since February; management assumes current prices for Q4 and says any worsening will hit margins.
Chinese diphenol/hydroquinone and vanillin oversupply and rerouting; anti-dumping duty dependence and reliance on distributors for vanillin volumes.
Working capital: management says the cycle is about 200 days, and the balance sheet relies on credit lines (about INR130 crore) during the liquidity squeeze.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the quarter, which management called not encouraging, attributing weakness to liquidity constraints, input cost inflation and local competition. Confident on recovery through the rights issue and the Q4 turnaround, but many forward numbers rely on assumptions rather than booked orders.
key_quotes: So it looks like we have to be -- we have to fight for this third quarter to stay afloat and at least give a similar result, we would have liked a much better EBITDA.
Q4 will be the first quarter with the liquidity with us. The turnaround will happen in Q4.
So our general working capital cycle is 200 days, and that's looking lower because we have INR130-odd crores of credit.
